description: EE migration replaces users_user_type_check so users.user_type accepts 'internal' | 'client' | 'service' (DROP CONSTRAINT, ADD … NOT VALID, VALIDATE; Citus-safe); CE constraint unchanged

EE migration creates service_principals(tenant, user_id, kind, name, description, allow_act_as, rate_limit_max_tokens, rate_limit_refill_per_min, created_by, archived_at, created_at, updated_at) with PK (tenant, user_id)
EE migration adds agents.service_user_id; all readers of metadata.backing_user_id switch to the column

EE migration adds nullable via-principal columns: time_entries.created_via_principal_id/updated_via_principal_id, time_sheets.approved_via_principal_id, schedule_entries/interactions/comments/project_tasks.created_via_principal_id, tickets.entered_via_principal_id, ticket_audit_logs.via_principal_user_id, mcp_agent_audit.act_as_user_id
CE enforce.ts / apiRateLimitConfigGetter honor a context-supplied rateLimitConfig override (generic; default unchanged)
EE migration adds nullable tenants.service_principal_limit (platform-admin override)
EE migration adds RBAC resource service_principal (read/create/update/delete) and seeds it to the Admin role
Shared TypeScript/Zod user-type unions in packages/types widened to include 'service' (vocabulary only; no CE code produces it); login/SSO/portal types stay internal|client
Stale API userTypeSchema (admin/contractor) corrected to internal|client|service; user create/update schemas accept only internal|client
packages/types exports isClientUserType, isMspPrincipalUserType, isInteractiveUserType, isLicensedUserType and INTERACTIVE_USER_TYPES
Portal 'require client' guards (~45 `!== 'client'` sites in client-portal actions/routes, extension proxies) converted to isClientUserType; service users are denied

MSP-data-scope sites converted to isMspPrincipalUserType (clients/projects/tickets list-search predicates, ticket/record visibility, ticketRecordAuthorization, commentActions client guard, documentAuthorization, invoiceQueries, TicketService.ts:396, policyActions.ts:146, userActions assertPortalUserManagementScope, quote sole-approver)
Session/UI sites converted to isInteractiveUserType (getSession, checkTrackedSession, express authMiddleware, middleware.ts portal routing, signin page, Header avatar)
addUser seat check (userActions.ts:557) keyed on isLicensedUserType
Authorization-subject normalizers map 'service' explicitly (authorizationKernel.ts:78, credentialAuthorization.ts:130, workflow crm.ts:969, projects.ts:1078)

CE comment author resolution (comment.ts:99,235, commentActions.ts:536, commentAuthorResolution.ts:61, optimizedTicketActions.ts:3450) treats a non-interactive author as a named non-human user, never client/contact; EE ServiceAuthorBadge slot adds the Service badge/avatar

Activity actor kind, mention-recipient kind and `|| 'internal'` defaults (latestActivityActor.ts, internalNotificationSubscriber, UserService, userActions, sessionActions) handle non-interactive types explicitly
User.getAll / getAllUsers / getAllUsersBasic return only interactive user types unless includeNonInteractive: true; userTypeFilter={null} pickers follow the same default
UserService list, search and user_type stats return only interactive user types by default

REST-reachable 'must be internal' checks that mean 'MSP-side caller' accept MSP principals (TicketService.ts:2785, taskCommentService.ts:83,172, ApiTimeSheetController, ApiTicketController, documents routes); human-meaning checks stay internal; classification recorded in SCRATCHPAD
Role assignment (policyActions.ts:453/457, roleActions.ts:106/110) lets an MSP principal type hold MSP roles and rejects client roles
RBAC resolution (three rbac.ts copies, search/acl.ts, tags/permissions.ts, user-composition/permissions.ts, kernel builtinProvider) uses isMspPrincipalUserType explicitly

EE createServicePrincipal (ee/server/src/lib/service-principals) creates the service user (locked sentinel password, name mirrored to first_name), service_principals row and MSP role grants in one transaction after the tier gate and checkServicePrincipalLimit
updateServicePrincipal edits name, description, roles and allow_act_as (allow_act_as requires service_principal:update); name stays mirrored to users.first_name
setServicePrincipalActive(false) sets users.is_inactive, agents.active=false (mcp_agent) and deactivates every active key owned by the principal in one transaction
Reactivating a service principal is limit-checked and does not revive previously deactivated keys

archiveOrDeleteServicePrincipal archives a referenced principal (deactivate, delete keys, set archived_at, clear IdP binding) and hard-deletes only an unreferenced one; mcp_agent_audit is never deleted

EE issueServicePrincipalKey writes a purpose='service' key owned by the principal directly (not via ApiKeyService.createApiKey), returns plaintext once; revoke and rotate (grace via expireApiKeyAfter)
listServicePrincipals returns non-archived principals with kind, roles, act-as flag, status, active key count and last used
No code path other than the service-principal service may insert or update a users row with user_type='service'
createAgent creates a kind='mcp_agent' service principal via createServicePrincipal and is checked against the service-principal limit, not seats
setAgentActive delegates to setServicePrincipalActive
deleteAgent delegates to archiveOrDeleteServicePrincipal; archived agent's (issuer, subject) can be bound to a new agent
resolveAgentByIdp and mintAgentSessionKey use agents.service_user_id; minting refuses an inactive service user
authenticateUser rejects non-interactive user types and requires an explicit userType (untyped User.findUserByEmail fallback removed)
NextAuth signIn callback calls assertInteractiveUser(userId, tenant) for every provider and returns false before recordLoginSuccess, enforceMaxSessions, updateLastLogin or session-row creation
checkTrackedSession, requireLiveSession and sessionAuthMiddleware share INTERACTIVE_USER_TYPES
Mobile handoff, issueMobileOtt, exchangeOttForSession and refreshMobileSession require an active internal user
Apple sign-in via an already-linked apple_user_identities row checks the user is active and internal
IAP restore/provision bind only to an active internal user
ApiKeyService.createApiKey stays internal-owner-only for every purpose (mobile_session, mcp_user, general); it never issues service keys

Password writes refuse non-interactive targets: adminChangeUserPassword, UserService password change, PasswordResetService.createResetToken, completePasswordReset, setNewPassword (untyped fallback removed)
ssoPreferences.ts untyped findUserByEmail lookup replaced with a typed internal lookup
Unused duplicate `export const options` / validateUser block in nextAuthOptions.ts removed after confirming no importers
Next middleware and msp/layout redirect a session with a non-interactive user type to sign-in rather than the client portal

CE buildAuthenticatedApiContext keeps the internal path and delegates non-internal, non-client owners to resolveServicePrincipalApiContext from @product/service-principals/entry; assertInternalApiUser becomes assertApiPrincipal (internal user or boundary-produced service context) at every caller
Both getKeyGateReason copies use an allow-list: active internal passes, client rejected, any other type passes only if the boundary's servicePrincipalKeyGate approves (CE stub rejects)

CE ApiContext gains generic principal {userId, userType, kind}, actAsUserId, effectiveUserId and rateLimitConfig fields defaulting to the key owner; context.userId means effective user; ApiKey type includes agent_id
CE ServiceContext carries viaPrincipalUserId and withViaPrincipal(ctx, row) adds via columns only when it is set

EE X-Alga-Act-As validation: principal must have allow_act_as (403 ACT_AS_NOT_ALLOWED), target an active internal user in tenant (422 ACT_AS_INVALID_TARGET); CE middleware rejects the header on human-owned keys (400 ACT_AS_NOT_SUPPORTED)
CE authorization kernel can authorize two subjects jointly (allow only if both allow, record rules evaluated for each); EE act-as uses it for RBAC intersection
assertHumanWorkAssignee(trx, tenant, userIds) guard rejects any non-active-internal id with HUMAN_WORK_ASSIGNEE_INVALID
Ticket assigned_to (create/update), addTicketResourceCore and assignTeamToTicketCore call the human-work guard
ScheduleEntry.create / updateAssignees call the human-work guard
Time-entry owner uses effectiveUserId; a non-internal effective user throws HumanWorkOwnerRequiredError, which EE maps to 422 ACT_AS_REQUIRED
Time-sheet owner and approve (approved_by) use effectiveUserId and the human-work guard; a bare service principal gets ACT_AS_REQUIRED
Time-entry approval requires a human approver (ACT_AS_REQUIRED for a bare service principal)
Project task assigned_to and task_resources call the human-work guard
Interaction owner uses effectiveUserId and the human-work guard
resolveScheduleAssignees never defaults the assignee to a non-internal caller; with no assignees the write throws HumanWorkOwnerRequiredError (EE: ACT_AS_REQUIRED)
Human-work guard validates only fields the write sets or changes; legacy references to former agent users don't block unrelated edits
Time-entry writers stamp created_via_principal_id / updated_via_principal_id from ServiceContext
Time-sheet approval stamps approved_via_principal_id
Schedule-entry and interaction writers stamp created_via_principal_id
Comment, ticket (entered_via_principal_id) and project-task writers stamp via-principal
ticket_audit_logs records actor_type='service_principal' (plain string column, no constraint change) when a principal acts as itself, and actor_type='user' + via_principal_user_id under act-as
Generic auditLog() records via_principal_user_id in details
MCP call meta-tool accepts act_as_user_id, forwards it as X-Alga-Act-As on the loopback dispatch and records it in mcp_agent_audit.act_as_user_id
CE ticket activity feed, time-entry detail and comment header render the EE ViaPrincipalLabel slot ('<human> via <principal>') when a via column is set
SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_ENTITLEMENT (Pro) in ee/server/src/lib/service-principals/entitlements.ts: maxPrincipals 10 (flat, not seat-scaled); default and ceiling rate limit 120 burst / 60 per min

Limit resolution: hosted → tenants.service_principal_limit else Pro default; appliance (license_state row) → verified signed service_principals claim else Pro default, ignoring tenants.service_principal_limit; unreadable/invalid token falls back to the Pro default, never unlimited; claim read in EE only
checkServicePrincipalLimit(trx, tenant) counts active (non-archived) service users and returns SERVICE_PRINCIPAL_LIMIT_REACHED at the limit; archiving frees the slot
EE boundary sets rateLimitSubjectId = sp:<principal user_id> for every service-principal request regardless of key (covers MCP per-request keys)

EE boundary sets rateLimitConfig from service_principals override → Pro default (a per-key api_rate_limit_settings row still wins); override capped at the Pro ceiling, raisable only by a hosted platform override
getServicePrincipalUsage(tenant) returns {limit, used, remaining}
EE AccountManagement page shows a service-principal usage row beside seats with 'don't use seats' note and settings link
Appliance LicenseManagementPage shows the service-principal usage row
Settings → Security → Service principals tab: DataTable (name, kind badge, roles, act-as, status, keys, last used, created by display name) with usage header and New disabled at limit
Create/Edit service principal dialog (name, description, MSP roles, allow act-as switch, optional rate-limit override within ceiling)
Manage keys dialog: issue (shown once), revoke, rotate
EE MCP server settings agent list/create use the service-principal backend and show the shared limit
Settings → Users MSP tab filters with isLicensedUserType; user detail loader rejects non-interactive ids
User server actions (adminChangeUserPassword, deleteUser, invite, reactivate) refuse non-interactive targets
API keys admin list renders an EE principal cell (name + Service badge) for principal-owned keys; CE stub falls back to today's rendering
user_type is immutable through REST UserService.update and user actions except existing internal↔client changes
REST UserService.create accepts only internal|client and runs checkInternalUserLicenseLimit for internal

EE data migration converts every agent's backing user to user_type='service', sets is_inactive = NOT agents.active, mirrors name, backfills agents.service_user_id and inserts service_principals (kind mcp_agent); idempotent, skips and logs missing/non-internal users
Migration never deactivates or deletes principals to fit the new limit; over-limit tenants only lose the ability to create
OpenAPI documents X-Alga-Act-As and the new error codes on affected routes; MCP and chat API registries regenerated
MCP call tool description documents act_as_user_id and ACT_AS_REQUIRED
New UI strings added to the msp settings locale files
TIER_FEATURES.SERVICE_PRINCIPALS added with FEATURE_MINIMUM_TIER 'pro' (namespace-member pattern like CREDENTIALS)

EE assertTenantTierAccess(SERVICE_PRINCIPALS) enforced in createServicePrincipal (covers createAgent), reactivation, issueServicePrincipalKey and enabling allow_act_as; below Pro returns 403 TIER_ACCESS_DENIED
Existing principals on a tenant below Pro (pre-existing or after downgrade) keep authenticating and resolving MCP tokens; only create/reactivate/key issuance is blocked; nothing is deactivated

Below Pro the Service principals tab and MCP agent create flow render TierGate / FeatureUpgradeNotice via useTierFeature; grandfathered principals stay listed with deactivate/delete only; license page row reads 'Available on Pro'

Static edition-boundary guard: fails if any file outside ee/, packages/product-service-principals/ or packages/ee/ references the service_principals table, X-Alga-Act-As, the 'service' key purpose or the service-principal entitlement

New packages/product-service-principals with oss/entry.ts (stubs: resolveServicePrincipalApiContext → null, servicePrincipalKeyGate → reject, error mapping pass-through) and ee/entry.ts re-exporting ee/server/src/lib/service-principals; aliased in server/next.config.mjs and server/tsconfig.json like @product/mcp/entry

CE stubs in packages/ee/src/components/service-principals (settings tab, usage row, ViaPrincipalLabel, ServiceAuthorBadge, API-key principal cell) render null; the Service principals settings tab is registered only when isEnterprise

EE resolveServicePrincipalApiContext validates an active non-archived principal, applies act-as, sets principal/actAsUserId/effectiveUserId/viaPrincipalUserId and the rate-limit subject/config, and maps HumanWorkOwnerRequiredError to ACT_AS_REQUIRED

EE server actions (ee/server/src/lib/actions/service-principal-actions.ts) for list/create/update/activate/archive/keys, each requiring an interactive internal session and the service_principal permission

Ticket-comment write core forces non-interactive authors to internal comments: unspecified visibility defaults to internal; explicit is_internal=false throws HumanWorkOwnerRequiredError('is_internal') (EE: 422 ACT_AS_REQUIRED); under act-as the human authors and public is allowed with created_via_principal_id stamped
